C0.quote: the goal is to select a committee (a subset) of k alternatives

C1.quote: we employ quantitative techniques that allow to measure the extent
C1.note: Most results are proportionality-degree guarantees, a quantitative version of axiomatic proportionality. Coded AX as primary, though WD fits partly. Appendix G gives utilitarian efficiency bounds (WD). LPs are used to bound guarantees, not to compute outcomes.

C2.1.value: approval-based profile; approval set; approval-based preferences
C2.1.quote: A is an approval-based profile (or, in short, a profile)

C2.2.quote: a function A : N → S(C) that maps each voter to a subset

C2.3.note: The input itself is described as voters' preferences, i.e. candidates they find acceptable. No separate held attitude is defined.

C2.4.quote: A(i) consists of candidates that voter i finds acceptable
C2.4.note: Approval sets are described as preferences or acceptability and the rule is applied to them directly. There is no statement about submission or reporting.

C4.1.quote: the total number of approvals that the candidates from the winning committee
C4.1.note: Utility and satisfaction are defined as numbers of approved committee members. Satisfaction is defined as the average number of representatives (Section 2.2).

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: We define the utilitarian efficiency of a rule as a lower bound
C5.1.note: Proportionality guarantees (representation of cohesive groups) and utilitarian efficiency are used.

C5.2.quote: The satisfaction of the group V from a committee W
C5.2.note: Evaluated on approval sets, with no statement relating them to held attitudes.
